points: Q3 volume and ARPU trends will show whether the 15% volume growth and 18% ARPU expansion from Q2 carried through the summer, or whether SMB marketplace softness is slowing the core business.

The print will reveal if transaction costs stay near the Q2 13.7% level and if adjusted EBITDA ex-interest income keeps growing at a triple-digit pace, which is the margin story behind the FY1/FY2 EPS inflection.

With consensus looking for FY1 EPS of $0.30 and FY2 EPS of $0.46, the release and any guidance will test whether double-digit revenue ex-interest growth can continue into Q4 and support the +60% year-two EPS estimate.
Management's update on the Nuvei acquisition—announced June 15—and any regulatory or closing conditions will be as important as the quarter, since the deal timeline shapes the forward setup.
Peer prints from JKHY, TOST and EVTC in the same week will offer read-throughs on SMB/checkout demand and processing volumes, but PAYO's specific long case rests on B2B and emerging-market momentum.
The Q3 result will clarify whether the Q2 net loss was deal-cost driven and whether underlying profitability is recovering, which matters for the premium 1.6x P/E valuation.
watch: Volume growth holds at or above 15% year-over-year — supports the long.
ARPU growth holds at or above 18% year-over-year — supports the long.
Transaction costs as a % of revenue stay below 14% — supports the long.
B2B volume growth stays above 40% year-over-year — supports the long.
